Executive SummaryPublic Sector ICT

ResQ-Gov is a mission-critical Digital Government command and logistics platform engineered for Regional Social Services Agencies (Dinas Sosial) and Disaster Management Agencies (BPBD). Unlike conventional government portals that function merely as passive data-entry spreadsheets, ResQ-Gov embeds 12 Binding Public-Sector Governance Rules (R-01 to R-12) directly into its state-transition engine.

By combining Segregation of Duties (SoD), Per-Capita Demographic Quota Capping, Zero-Trust 6-Digit Handover OTPs, and an Append-Only Cryptographic Hash-Chain Audit Trail, ResQ-Gov eliminates phantom aid requisitions, prevents political hoarding, accelerates emergency dispatch within a 1-to-6-hour SLA, and guarantees 100% auditability for Supreme Audit Institution (BPK RI) inspections.

Four-Pillar Governance ArchitectureAPICTA Standard
  • Pillar 1 — Executive Command & Multi-Tier Approval (R-01, R-02): Enforces strict actor separation between Camp Requestor, Warehouse Verifier, and Head of Agency Approver (mandatory for requisitions > IDR 25,000,000).
  • Pillar 2 — Mathematical Quota & Stock Reservation (R-03, R-04): Caps aid requests dynamically based on verified camp headcounts (max 3-day consumption norm) minus in-flight quantities.
  • Pillar 3 — Last-Mile Custody & Discrepancy Detection (R-05, R-06): Requires a secret 6-digit camp OTP upon truck arrival (3-strike lock) followed by itemized physical count verification.
  • Pillar 4 — Tamper-Evident Forensic Ledger (R-09, R-10): Chains every state mutation into an immutable hash sequence (prevHash → hash), instantly exposing any database tampering.

Section 02 Problem Statement — Systemic Failures in Public Disaster Logistics
Category 02: Public Sector & Government
02

Problem Statement

Why Legacy Disaster Relief Administration Fails Citizens During the Critical 72-Hour Golden Window

2.1 Empirical Context: The Indonesian Disaster Logistics Paradox

Situated along the Pacific Ring of Fire and subject to intensifying monsoon extremes, Indonesia records over 3,000 natural disasters annually (BNPB Disaster Data, 2024–2026), displacing millions of citizens across floods, landslides, earthquakes, and volcanic eruptions. During the first 72 hours (the humanitarian Golden Window), survival depends not merely on the existence of national relief stockpiles, but on the speed, mathematical equity, and custodial integrity of last-mile distribution executed by Regional Social Services Agencies (Dinas Sosial) and Regional Disaster Management Agencies (BPBD).

Paradoxically, post-disaster evaluations consistently reveal that while district warehouses (Gudang Induk) hold sufficient buffer stocks of rice, medicines, and shelter kits, field evacuation camps (Posko Pengungsian) suffer simultaneous acute stockouts, severe over-hoarding, and unverified cargo disappearance. Existing government software tools fail because they are built as passive reporting forms rather than rule-enforcing governance engines.

2.2 Four Root Causes of Public Sector Logistics Failure

1. Information Asymmetry & Sensus BlindspotsLatency

Field officers report evacuee headcounts via fragmented WhatsApp messages and paper tables. Command centers lack real-time visibility into camp saturation or vulnerable sub-populations (infants needing MP-ASI formula, elderly requiring chronic medication, pregnant women, and persons with disabilities). Stale census data leads to severe supply mismatches.

2. Panic Hoarding & "Ghost Evacuee" InflationInequity

In the absence of mathematical per-capita quota enforcement, vocal or easily accessible camps submit inflated requisitions—stockpiling weeks of food reserves—while isolated rural shelters face starvation. Duplicate requests submitted across shifts drain central warehouses within hours.

3. Collapsed Segregation of Duties (SoD)Corruption Risk

Under emergency pressure, the same official often initiates, verifies, and approves high-value aid releases without multi-tier oversight. Paper-based handover receipts (Berita Acara Serah Terima / BAST) are routinely signed in bulk, backdated, or falsified by transit personnel without physical verification by camp recipients.

4. Unmonitored SLAs & Modifiable Audit LogsAudit Failure

Traditional spreadsheets and standard CRUD databases allow retroactive editing or deletion of transaction records after discrepancies occur. Consequently, Supreme Audit Institution (BPK RI) and Inspectorate audits frequently issue formal findings over unaccounted emergency contingency budgets (Belanja Tidak Terduga / BTT).

2.3 Structural Failure Cascade (Traditional Paper & Chat Workflow)

Section 04 Proposed Solution — Code-Enforced Governance & Mathematical Rule Engine
Category 02: Public Sector & Government

Proposed Solution

End-to-End Disaster Logistics State Machine & The 12 Code-Enforced Governance Rules (R-01 to R-12)

4.1 Architectural Breakthrough: Governance-as-Code

ResQ-Gov transforms disaster relief from an informal administrative workflow into a deterministic, cryptographically verifiable state machine. Every mutation must pass through a centralized validation kernel (src/rules/businessRules.ts & src/store/StoreContext.tsx); any rule violation is blocked at runtime and recorded as a flagged anomaly in the hash-chained audit ledger.

4.2 Complete Specification of the 12 Enforced Business Rules (R-01 to R-12)

Rule Governance Principle Statutory & Operational Rule Specification Code-Level Enforcement Mechanism
R-01 Segregation of Duties (SoD) Requestor, Verifier, and Approver must be distinct officers. Drivers cannot confirm final receipt. Runtime actor check (actor.id !== req.requestedBy); self-approval blocked & logged.
R-02 Multi-Tier Executive Approval Requisitions valued > IDR 25,000,000 require digital approval from Head of Agency after Coordinator check. Auto-transitions to menunggu_persetujuan; dispatch blocked until admin approves.
R-03 Demographic Norm Quota Cap Requested qty capped at per-capita norm (max 3-day coverage) minus active in-flight requests for the camp. Ceiling maxAllowedQty(item, post) - inFlightQty(...) enforced on submission.
R-04 Warehouse Stock & Reservation Cannot verify or dispatch if unreserved warehouse stock is insufficient. Stock auto-deducts on dispatch. Checks availableQty = stock - reservedQty; creates immutable outbound MOV record.
R-05 6-Digit OTP Handover Proof Each shipment has a secret 6-digit code known only to destination Posko. Driver must input code on arrival. 3 failed attempts lock shipment (locked = true) & alert Coordinator.
R-06 Physical Receipt & Discrepancy Posko Officer records actual physical qty received per item. If receivedQty < qty, status becomes selisih. Raises red executive alert on Kepala Dinas dashboard until Berita Acara resolution.
R-07 Service Level Agreement (SLA) Darurat: ≤1h verify / ≤6h deliver; Tinggi: ≤3h / ≤12h; Normal: ≤6h / ≤24h. Live countdown timer getSla(req, now) flags overdue items & historical breaches.
R-08 Mandatory Documentary Evidence Rejections require ≥20-char reason; requests require ≥30-char justification; stock-in requires BAST ref. Form & store mutations reject payloads failing length or BAST reference checks.
R-09 Tamper-Evident Audit Hash Chain Every state change & violation is appended to an immutable log hashing its payload + prevHash. No edit/delete API; verifyAuditChain() detects any modified or deleted block.
R-10 Evacuee Data Freshness & Surge Posko must update evacuees within 24h before requesting aid. Changes >30% or over capacity are flagged. Blocks requests if now - post.lastUpdate > 24h; sets flagged: true on surge logs.
R-11 Session & Account Security Auto-logout after 30 mins idle. 5 failed logins lock account 15 mins. Min 1 active Admin required. Enforced by auth guard; prevents disabling the last active Kepala Dinas account.
R-12 Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) Each user accesses only routes & data scoped to their assignment (Posko own camp; Driver own vehicle). Dual-layer enforcement in router (App.tsx) and store runner (run(roles, fn)).

4.3 Core Mathematical Models Enforced by the Engine

Rule R-03: Net Requestable Quota per Item (i) at Camp (p)
Q_max(i, p) = ceil( Evacuees(p) × Norm(i) × D(i) ) - Q_inflight(i, p)
where D(i) = 3 days if normBasis == 'hari', else 1 (durable)
Rule R-09: Consecutive Cryptographic Audit Block Hash (seq = k)
H_k = Hash( seq_k | ts_k | actor_k | role_k | action_k | target_k | detail_k | flag_k | H_{k-1} )
where H_0 = "00000000000000" (Genesis Block Anchor)

Key Features & Tech Stack

Six Mission-Critical Functional Modules & High-Performance Zero-Overhead Web Architecture

5.1 Six Core Functional Modules

1. Executive Policy & Multi-Tier Approval CockpitAdmin

Provides the Head of Agency with real-time KPI telemetry (Pending High-Value Approvals, Open Physical Discrepancy Cases, Total Registered Evacuees, and Realized Aid Budget in IDR), regional food/medical stockpile resilience area charts, and a 1-click executive authorization desk for requisitions exceeding IDR 25,000,000.

2. Interactive GIS Crisis & Radar Command CenterSpatial GIS

Custom zero-latency SVG geospatial command map visualizing watershed hazard zones (Zona Bahaya Longsor & Banjir DAS), evacuation post capacity saturation rings, central Pusdalops warehouse nodes, and live GPS fleet route progress (0–100% with dynamic ETA). Includes a live disaster event simulator & dynamic field post registration.

3. Demographic Norm & Quota Requisition EnginePosko

Tracks camp headcounts and 4 vulnerable groups (Balita, Lansia, Disabilitas, Ibu Hamil). Automatically computes remaining allowable quotas across 9 standardized relief items (Rice 0.4 kg/person/day, Clean Water 2.5 L/day, Instant Noodles 2 packs/day, Medical Kits, Masks, Tents, Blankets, Hygiene Kits, Infant MP-ASI).

4. Warehouse Inventory & Fleet Capacity DispatcherKoordinator

Separates physical stock from reserved stock (availableQty = stock - reservedQty), triggers low-stock alerts below minimum thresholds, logs inbound donor consignments with mandatory BAST references, and assigns approved shipments to available fleet vehicles (Pick-up 1,000 kg, Truk Engkel 4,000 kg, Truk Fuso 8,000 kg).

5. Zero-Trust 6-Digit OTP Handover & ReconciliationDriver & Posko

Eliminates transit fraud by requiring the driver to input the destination Posko's secret 6-digit OTP upon arrival. Three failed attempts lock the shipment immediately. Once unlocked/delivered, the Posko Officer performs itemized physical reconciliation, automatically escalating any shortage to SELISIH status.

6. Cryptographic Audit Verifier & Official BAST ExportCompliance

Displays every historical action, actor NIP, timestamp, and cyrb53 cryptographic hash link. Includes an interactive "Uji Integritas Rantai" verifier that validates every block from Genesis (00000000000000), plus print-ready official government BAST reports and one-click CSV forensic exports.

Competitive Advantage

How ResQ-Gov Outperforms Legacy Manual Workflows, Commercial ERPs, and Static E-Gov Portals

7.1 Multi-Dimensional Competitive Matrix

Existing disaster logistics approaches fall into three categories: (1) ad-hoc WhatsApp groups and Excel spreadsheets, (2) heavy commercial Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) suites (e.g., SAP, Oracle, Odoo), or (3) basic government web forms that lack business-rule validation. ResQ-Gov bridges this gap by combining lightweight, rapid-deployment web engineering with strict public-sector statutory enforcement:

Business Model

Sustainable B2G & B2B2G Revenue Streams, E-Katalog LKPP Procurement & Fiscal Savings Analysis

9.1 Public-Sector Business Model Canvas (B2G + B2B2G Hybrid)

To ensure rapid institutional adoption without burdening local governments with prohibitive upfront capital expenditure, ResQ-Gov operates a Dual-Track GovTech Sustainability Model compliant with Indonesian public procurement regulations (E-Katalog LKPP):

Stream 1: Regency B2G SaaS60% Revenue

Annual Subscription & Managed Cloud/PDN Support: Priced at IDR 75,000,000 / year / Regency (Kabupaten/Kota) covering unlimited ASN users, evacuation camps, and fleet vehicles. Funded via annual APBD Dinsos/BPBD operational ICT budgets or Belanja Tidak Terduga (BTT) preparedness allocations.

Stream 2: Provincial Command25% Revenue

Provincial Multi-Regency Integration License: Priced at IDR 250,000,000 / year / Province (or subsidized via BNPB Dana Siap Pakai grants). Enables provincial governors and Pusdalops to monitor cross-district buffer stocks, mutual-aid transfers, and regional SLA compliance.

Stream 3: B2B2G CSR Portal15% Revenue

Corporate Philanthropy & ESG Audit Gateway: Priced at IDR 35,000,000 / year / Enterprise Donor. Enables FMCG, telecom, and banking CSR donors to track their donated BAST batches down to verified camp handovers for ESG sustainability reporting.

9.2 Value-for-Money & Fiscal Return on Investment (ROI) for a Single Regency

An average disaster-prone regency manages IDR 5,000,000,000 in annual emergency logistics and social relief supplies across flood and landslide seasons. By eliminating phantom requisitions, duplicate hoarding, and unverified transit shrinkage (conservatively estimated at 15–20% in manual systems), ResQ-Gov pays for its annual subscription more than 10 times over in a single disaster response cycle:

Impact Plan

Measurable Humanitarian, Fiscal Governance, and Sustainable Development Impact

10.1 Three-Dimensional Public Impact Framework

1. Humanitarian & Citizen Survival
85% Faster
Emergency Verification & Dispatch

Compresses emergency aid verification to ≤ 1 hour and physical delivery to ≤ 6 hours (Rule R-07), preventing secondary mortality, dehydration, and untreated injuries in isolated evacuation camps. Explicit tracking of balita, lansia, disabilitas, and ibu hamil guarantees life-saving nutritional prioritization.

2. Anti-Corruption & Clean Audit
100% Traceable
Cryptographic Chain of Custody

Eliminates "ghost camps" and phantom deliveries through mathematical quota ceilings (R-03), dual-key 6-digit OTP handovers (R-05), and append-only hash chaining (R-09). Directly supports regional governments in retaining WTP (Wajar Tanpa Pengecualian) audit opinions from BPK RI.

3. Operational & Green GovTech
90% Paperless
Digital BAST & Fleet Efficiency

Replaces multi-carbon paper Surat Jalan and manual ledger books with instant digital BAST generation and CSV audit exports. Capacity-matched fleet dispatching prevents overloaded truck breakdowns and reduces unnecessary fuel consumption across hazardous routes.

10.3 Alignment with United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)

SDG 11.5 — Disaster ResilienceGoal 11

"Significantly reduce the number of deaths and the number of people affected and substantially decrease the direct economic losses relative to global GDP caused by disasters, with a focus on protecting the poor and people in vulnerable situations."

SDG 16.5 & 16.6 — Accountable GovGoal 16

"Substantially reduce corruption and bribery in all their forms" and "Develop effective, accountable and transparent institutions at all levels" through code-enforced Segregation of Duties and immutable cryptographic audit logs.

SDG 2.1 & 3.8 — Nutrition & HealthGoals 2 & 3

Guarantees equitable daily caloric access (0.4 kg rice, 2.5 L clean water, infant MP-ASI) and essential emergency medical/hygiene kits for displaced populations during acute climate shocks.

Roadmap & Future Direction

Strategic Evolution from Regency Command Platform to AI-Predictive & ASEAN Interoperable Ecosystem

11.1 Multi-Horizon Strategic & Engineering Roadmap (2026–2028+)

11.2 Deep-Dive into Upcoming Technological Innovations

1. Zero-Internet LoRa & Satellite Mesh FallbackResilience

Major earthquakes and flash floods frequently sever cellular base stations (BTS). In Horizon 1–2, ResQ-Gov introduces a Progressive Web App (PWA) CRDT offline queue paired with compact LoRaWAN/Starlink Direct-to-Cell gateways, allowing Posko officers and drivers to verify 6-digit HMAC-TOTP handover codes completely offline and sync the hash chain once connectivity returns.

2. AI Predictive Demand & Pre-Positioning EngineArtificial Intelligence

By ingesting live BMKG rainfall radar, watershed river-gauge telemetry, and historical camp inflow rates, our upcoming AI Pre-Positioning Module forecasts 72-hour commodity depletion before stockouts occur—automatically recommending pre-emptive buffer transfers from neighboring district warehouses.

3. BSrE-BSSN Certified Electronic Signatures (TTE)Legal Validity

Integrating Balai Sertifikasi Elektronik (BSrE - BSSN) PKI certificates directly into Rule R-02 (Kepala Dinas approval) and Rule R-06 (Official BAST PDF generation), giving every exported ResQ-Gov document full statutory evidentiary force under Indonesia's ITE Law.

4. Cross-Border ASEAN Interoperability (AHA Centre)Regional Scale

Standardizing commodity taxonomy and hash-chain manifest schemas to interoperate with the Disaster Emergency Logistics System for ASEAN (DELSA) operated by the AHA Centre, enabling seamless cross-border humanitarian relief tracking across Southeast Asia.

National Policy Vision: Towards a Unified Indonesian Disaster Logistics Ledger

Our long-term direction positions ResQ-Gov as the reference open-standard logistics governance module within Indonesia’s National Public Service Portal (INA Digital / SPBE)—connecting 514 regencies into a single, mathematically governed national resilience network where no displaced citizen is left behind and every Rupiah of humanitarian aid is cryptographically accountable.
